_comment: Per-level conversion spec. Holds ONLY our own choices and indexes into the user's disc (string ordinals in DATA/chars.bum, stream indexes in banks, segment numbers in main.mus) - never Frontline text or data. The converter resolves them on the player's PC and writes the result into the generated pk3 only.

1_1.place: Pointe Saint-Mathieu (St. Mathieu), Finistere, Brittany, France
1_1._place_source: disc: briefing journal 1_1_bLog.viv page j1_1_pg1 header 'SEASIDE STOWAWAY / St. Mathieu, France / 17 August 1944 - 0900 Hours'; location table chars.bum @0x2bd0 (= shell.viv @0x10a36d0). Real place: Pointe Saint-Mathieu lighthouse/abbey near Brest - matches the dock dialogue about docking near the lighthouse. No St. Nazaire / St. Malo / Periers strings on the disc; the 'Periers 7 km' road sign is level-only dressing art, not the setting. Levels 1_3/1_4 = 'Shipyards of Lorient, France'. Chrono: before AA M5 (20 Aug 1944, Brest).

[flfix2 bug-11080] set-piece keys parent/after/hold/stop: a child runs on its parent's clock - made 'after' seconds after the parent starts, waits 'hold', and stops 'stop' seconds into its own keys (emulator trace of the bomber pass, TRACE_bombers.md: bombs made at +153 and +219 ticks, on the ground at +261 and +309, the house goes at +303)
1_1._motion_first: [flpolish] the key a motion starts from, named outright (else flpack's collision sweep picks the first key whose run is open). The jeep starts at Frontline's own key 1 behind the farm gate again: it used to be forced to key 20 because a start past x 8192 was never drawn - the entity-origin wire format wraps at +-8192 (bug-flp-jeepdraw); the converter now opts the map into the HZM engine's wide coordinates (worldspawn hzm_widecoords).

1_1._set_pieces: [flpolish] which Frontline motion plays when, and as what: 'mesh' = Frontline's own object mesh from the player's disc (flconvert builds it as an inline model), 'model' = a stock MOHAA stand-in when there is none. 'trigger'/'object' are Frontline RECORD indexes resolved on the player's PC. Planes go to the trigger their flight passes closest to (unique assignment; the untriggered start pass and the two dogfights open over the drop); bombs and rockets to the triggers that send them; the house chunks fall when the second bomb lands beside them (its fall is 3.4 s); the jeep's wheels fly off on the jeep's own clock from the mine hit ('sync'); the U-boat bobs all mission.

Signs, house fronts and anything with a feature at a fixed place are never listed. Tried and withdrawn after review (kept original): cobbles 54200 and b3600 (replacement read as a clean regular sett grid), stone wall 4aa80 (rubble versus the original's coursed blocks).

1_1._oneshots_events: [decodeaudit 2026-11-23, gap 5, bug-11478] DECODED, replaces the transcription table above (kept for reference, unused while events is set): the soldiers' voice behaviour 2 (SoldierA_Roamer L0040) sends AEMSEVENT {module 15 = the area LOAD bank's bark module, event, speaker type}; the bank's graph picks a sample range per event and voice family (flaudio.bark_slots). Events by sender: 1 hit (pain run 1, b1 hit reactions / event 47), 2 death (pain run 2, b0 states 26 / 70), 3 attack start (b0 state 41 / b1 L056d), 4 move to a cover point (b0 state 58), 5 cover point re-picked (b0 states 49-53), 7 Alert entry and the squad-signal anims (b0 L1250 / L1626, b1 states 290 / 397 / 465 / 553); 6 Curious, 8 run to alarm, 9, 10 have no live clip on 1_1 (silent). German family: events 1-5, 7; American family: 3-5. Names = our aivoice situations (contact = 7 Alert entry, attack = 3, cover = 4, fallback = 5); 1 / 2 stay with the engine pain / death sounds (the mission never played any_pain). Situations the original has no event for (suppress, backup, banter, kill, mandown, taunt, reload) stay silent.
1_1._prop_sounds: [decodeaudit 2026-11-23, bug-11479] SOMI rows of the records' own PLAYSOUND ids: plane = every FlyThrough_1_1 (recs 287-292, 301; PLAYSOUND 66 at the start of its pass, set 450 sub 746 -> entry 21, a 7.5 s flyby; sub 747 holds the same entry); jeep = JeepBody_1_1 rec 277 (PLAYSOUND 66 as it starts, set 452 -> entry 29, 10.1 s); tank_hit = TankVehicle rec 252 PLAYSOUND 61 on a heavy hit (set 519 -> entries 17-18; the first is taken, the random pick between the two is not). Distances (min / max) are ours: the SOMI row carries none we read. [decodeaudit r100, aems / senders] every row takes ALL its entries first..last with its pitch range (tank_hit: entries 17 / 18 at 50 / 50, pitch 3300..3700 / 4096 -> 0.806 + 0.098). tank_turret = PLAYSOUND 74 of set 519 (NOT the cannon): the turret-traverse loop, entry 30 (ScrBnk slot 62, a 1.416 s loop), volume 0.977, pitch 1.0; started by HierobjVehicle behaviour 1 state 3 on each turret-rotate command (209/3), ended at rotation done (209/4). Its range field 512 falls the ScrBnk distance table 0x941 to 0 at 22784 / 512 = 44.5 m (2136 u). mg_grunt = PLAYSOUND 82 of set 454 (no placed record links it: the jeep gunner's class set), run 3 entries 3..5 (s_56..58), pitch 0.93..1.07, volume 0.79, non-positional on the disc; played on the tick of the gunner's line (clip 6507 c80f 2).
1_1._vehicle_engines: [decodeaudit 2026-11-23, gap 11, bug-11479] the Panzer (TankVehicle rec 252, vehicle type 1 = TankVehicle behaviour 1 state 5) runs its engine from the start of its path to its death; 11VehBnk module 16 gives type 1 an idle loop (slot 0, 14.1 s) and a drive loop (slot 14, 16.1 s). Types 2 / 3 (HierobjVehicle / GunVehicle) have empty slots on 1_1, and the jeep (JeepBody_1_1, an AnimatedMovingMech) never reaches its engine-sound code: the jeep is silent in the original. The two gear-change one-shots (slots 8 / 21) and the running level that drives the gates and the pitch table (GETSOUNDINFO(3, 5)) are not converted. [decodeaudit r100, aems] the module's arguments are sent ONCE at begin and never updated (bp_tank.log: running level 8, 49.1 m; no AEMSEVENT(2) sender): at level 8 BOTH loops play for the tank's whole life - idle at pitch 1.0 (constant), drive at 0x12e7[8] = 2719 / 4096 = 0.664 - and the gear one-shots never fire. Volume frozen at begin: 32000 / 32767 x T1314(49.1 m) = 0.253. level / begin_dist_m derive both from the bank's own tables (flaudio.vehicle_params). min 3072 / max 3120 = positional with no rolloff out to 64 m, where T1314 reaches 0 (aems option A; the original's pan is frozen at begin too, ours follows the tank: listed). The loops are decoded as their exact loop bodies (2.027 s / 3.065 s).
1_1._impacts: [decodeaudit r100, senders 3a / 3b] the disc's bullet impacts (ImpBnk module 3, event 1 by surface) and fly-bys (module 5) in place of the stock families the cgame plays by surface type (1-based ImpBnk streams = banks/11ImpBnk_NN numbering). Keyed to the converter's surface types (footsteps): rock = materials 0 / 2 / 3 / 10 / 13 and untagged -> the hard set 38-47 (the disc's stone and untagged sound; ALSO snd_b_ricochet, the mod's hard-surface whine); dirt = 5 / 6 / 12 -> 27-31; metal = 7 / 8 / 9 -> 32 / 33 (the disc layers the hard set on half the metal hits: one alias per hit here, listed); wood = 1 / 4 / 11 -> 34-36; flesh -> 21-23; fly-by -> 01-08 (slots 9-16 of its set are empty on 1_1: the disc's ~half silent whizzes are not reproduced, listed). Not taken: glass 25 (the mat-13 panes are rock), mat 10's 24 and mat 3's silence (they share rock), the river (silent on the disc; the canal bed stays the stock puddle). Distance table 0x660: 2 m per entry, 0 at 62 m (94 % at 18 m, half at ~40 m) -> 720 / 2976; FL picks the pitch in 0.95..1.07. The families are left out of the alias bridge.
1_1._anim_sounds: [decodeaudit r100, senders 2] the converted clips' own sound opcodes (c80f n -> 1_1animSnd.som row n, a 'SOMA' table of 4 rows, all script bank run 1): flanimconv writes `sound fl11_anim<n>` on the clip's frame; flpack defines the alias (a row whose sample is a cue reuses the cue file). 1_1: clip 6507 (the gunner's rise) frame 0 c80f 2 = entry 18 = the 'mg_hurt' line. c806 (GunBnk foley) is in none of the converted clips.
1_1._oneshots: [flfix2 round 20] LoadOneShotSound areas (recs 53-59, bank n = record word 14): bank entry numbers per side_situation, OUR table, made 2026-11-13 by transcribing the decoded clips locally (faster-whisper small, German and English; H:/hzm_work/sweep_2026-11-13/sopfx/oneshot, never shipped). Each bank: entry 1 silence (dropped), about 20 pain grunts (any_pain, side unknown), then German lines, then American lines (the area's ALLIED barks too). de_* -> German AI, us_* -> allied AI, situations as coop_mod/aivoice.scr names them (contact, cover, attack, suppress, fallback, backup, banter = lost contact, kill, mandown, taunt, reload) plus grenade (no aivoice situation). Clips the transcript could not place are left out (46 of 431). [flfix2 round 22] the 37 voiced clips round 20 left out as unclear, and the 2 cries next to the pain run (1:22 = 5:21, one clip), placed: re-transcribed with faster-whisper small (beam 5, a German / English combat-phrase prompt, side from the clip's place in its bank) and checked against the placed sets' audio statistics (cries 0.24-0.67 s, one envelope peak, like the pain run; voiced lines 0.6-1.3 s, 2-6 peaks, like the speech sets). Our classification, low confidence where the words stay unclear (listed in FIDELITY round 22). The 7 entry-1 clips are digital silence (rms 0) and stay out. [decodeaudit r100, barks] events 1 / 2 (hit / death) are live in every bank and are the disc's own pain and death cries: the graph plays them from the GERMAN family for every speaker (table 1962 -> constant 099b = 1), so only 'de' carries them and the mission plays de_hit / de_death for both sides. dist = the bark graph's distance -> volume table 099d: 11Load1 falls almost linearly to 0 at 39 m (half at 16 m), 11Load2-9 hold full volume to 10 m and reach 0 at 70 m (half at 44 m).

generate._look_doc: [look 2026-11-16] every generated smoke / pall: the disc size is relative to its own smoke sprite, not metres (read as metres the house smoke and the burning-car smoke drew small opaque near-black blobs; the original plume is several metres wide, soft, dark grey: ref_xemu/trace/b41h_prepost.png). look = per-type default (size_k x size, grow = end / start size over the life, alpha, color_k lifts the colour); rec = per-record override; flames untouched

1_1._particles: [flfix2 round 20] Frontline placed particle systems (.bpd kind 9, flscene.particle) -> stock MOHAA emitters by decoded type (flpack._particles): smoke = rises steadily, grey; pall = big, black, hangs (sinks as well as rises); flame = orange start colour; blast = one-shot burst or scripted explosion class. start: record -> our reading where the record's own start field (word 32 high half: 1 load, 2 event) is not enough: 8 = the house smoke, which the original shows only after the house blast (ref_xemu/trace/b41h_prepost.png); 51 = StartBeachExplosionBig, listed with bomb A's blast set in the AUDIT (its starter on link 6:240 is not identified). life: seconds the stand-in stays for a burst (51: its four by-type systems + the 20-tick follow-up live up to 7.1 s). generate [flfix2 round 22]: every non-blast system gets its own emitter models/emitters/fl_<level>_pfx<rec>.tik in the converted pak (flpack.pfx_tik) with the decoded start / end size, rate, life, colour, box, velocity, acceleration and spin; sprites = the mod's stand-ins (the disc's are not on the level), sprite_px = their width in pixels (256: cfx_puff / cfx_flame images), alpha per type is ours (not decoded), rate0 = the rate used where the record's is 0 (recs 421 / 422 flame bed).

1_3._mesh_light: [data13 2026-11-23 MEASURED] 1.0: object meshes draw with the world's vertex program (oD0 = v3, combiner texture x colour, no x2) and their guest-RAM copies hold the disc's raw colours, so they take the same factor as the world
1_3._untextured_grey: [data13 2026-11-23 MEASURED] 255 = white x vertex colour, as the original: its untextured draws use combiner ICW 0x04200000 (vertex colour x 1); raw colours 67.6 mean vs 93.7 under a texture, so they read brighter than textured surfaces in the original too. The earlier 76 was a look fit (deviation removed)

1_3._glass: [data13 2026-11-23] game-drawn window panes (flglass.py): 1_3's are material 12 + special (1_1: 13); emulator GPU frame gpu_fl13g: 28 opaque quads on exactly those collision vertices, texture 1_3_ART.cpt@61480 (two-panel window), s = pane width / 3.1 m (a 1.5 m pane takes one half), t 0..1.
